📖 Game script

In London at 06:30 PT, Washington starts Marcus Mariota with Jayden Daniels out, Terry McLaurin doubtful and Rachaad White out. Bookmaker had pulled the Mariota, McLaurin and Jacory Croskey-Merritt prop menus at its 10/03 capture, which says the book itself isn't sure what this offense looks like. Indianapolis loses Keenan Allen (out on the 10/03 ESPN feed), so the targets concentrate on Josh Downs (72+ receiving yards at −106) and Tyler Warren (54+ at −105) on a MEDIUM secondary grade against a defense allowing 6.4 yards per play. Jonathan Taylor (91+ rushing at −102) runs into the Washington run defense the WAS backers lean on, so the Colts win through the air. Indianapolis by six: a cover of −4.5 by a point and a half, 46 total points.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

Experts split 7–4 toward Washington: Action Network ("Mariota is a top-tier backup"), BettingPros, Ross Tucker and Doug Kezirian at +3.5, PFF and Travis Pulver of BettingPros on the moneyline, and Mike Florio (Commanders 24–20) on WAS; Brandon Anderson, Andrew Erickson and Jason Logan at −3.5 and Ian Undery of Action Network on the moneyline for IND. Dave Tuley of VSiN passes. The line has moved from the Action Network open of IND −3.5 to −4.5. Splits: WAS has 68% of spread tickets but only 58% of the money; the IND moneyline has 70% of tickets and 83% of the money, short of a 15-point sharp gap. The projection (IND by 6) disagrees with the expert majority, but only by a point and a half against the number, so the lean is to pass the side and play the receiver: Brandon Anderson and Andrew Erickson both have Downs over 62.5 receiving, noting Washington has allowed the most wide-receiver fantasy points. The projected 46 sits a point under the 47 total; The over has four backers (BettingPros and Zachary Cohen of VSiN at 46.5, Ian Undery at 49.5, and a betting-trends account on X), mostly on the same 15–1 trend when Washington is a 3.5- to 9.5-point underdog. With the projection a point under and a first-half under system in Evan Abrams' primer, no total. Card: no ticket touches this game. The projection (IND by 6) and the 7–4 expert lean to Washington point opposite ways, so the card passes the side and the receiving props.

⚠️ What breaks it

Mariota runs well and Croskey-Merritt controls the clock, holding the Colts to field goals. McLaurin plays through the doubtful tag. Indianapolis is −5 in turnover margin through three games, so two giveaways turn a six-point Colts win into a Washington cover. Recheck inactives at about 05:00 PT.

🎙️ What the experts are saying

Washington side: seven sources.

Ross Tucker (Even Money): WAS +3.5 for 1 unit, Tue 9/29. He "believes the win over Seattle changes the dynamic for Washington." The current +4.5 is a point better than his number.

Doug Kezirian: WAS +3.5: "I'll gladly take the three and a half with Washington because I think they can win outright."

Action Network: WAS +3.5: "Mariota is a top-tier backup, Washington's run defense is elite, and 3.5 provides good line value against an overvalued Colts team."

BettingPros: WAS +3.5, twice. The neutral-site game lets "Washington's run defense contain Jonathan Taylor," and "Marcus Mariota looks competent driving the offense; line should be closer to a pick 'em."

Mike Florio (Pro Football Talk): Washington to win outright, 24–20.

PFF: the Washington moneyline, "an intriguing spot for the Commanders on the moneyline and in the alternate markets."

Travis Pulver (BettingPros): Commanders moneyline at +160.

Indianapolis side: four sources.

Andrew Erickson: IND −3.5, one of his 10 best bets. Washington's defense "is extremely poor," and the Colts' coach is 2–0 straight up and against the spread in international games, while Washington's staff and Mariota have struggled abroad.

Brandon Anderson: IND −3.5, also his contest pick: "Colts are the better team, best run blocking line, and Washington defense is weak."

Jason Logan: IND −3.5, Mon 9/28: "Commanders in a nasty letdown spot sandwich traveling to UK for their 3rd away game in first 4 weeks."

Ian Undery (Action Network): the Colts on the moneyline, with the over at 49.5.

No play. Dave Tuley (VSiN) passes on this game.

Total. BettingPros has over 46.5 ("both defenses have major flaws"), as do Zachary Cohen of VSiN and a betting-trends account on X; both note the over is 15–1 since 2024 when Washington is a 3.5- to 9.5-point underdog.

Props. Josh Downs over 62.5 receiving from Brandon Anderson and Andrew Erickson (Washington has "allowed the most fantasy points to WRs"). Rich Hribar's best-bets pick is Tyler Warren over 46.5: Warren plays "87% of the Colts' dropbacks" with a 23% target share, against a secondary 29th in completion rate allowed. PropStarz takes Jonathan Taylor under 90.5 rushing because of the Washington run defense. The two overs on Keenan Allen (Dave at 36.5 yards, Sal Bets at 3.5 catches) came before Allen was ruled out and no longer apply. Grant Neiffer has Daniel Jones to score at +400 and Terry McLaurin at +250 (McLaurin is doubtful).
